sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) An individual who initiates, creates and manages a new business is called an ________. (b) Entrepreneurship is a ________ activity.
Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Entrepreneurs are gamblers. (b) An entrepreneur generates employment for others.
questions.answer:
(a) False — they take calculated risks.
(b) True

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Only rich persons can start a business. (b) An entrepreneur should start a retail business far away from customers' residences.
questions.answer:
(a) False — anyone can start a small business.
(b) False — a retail shop should be near residential areas or a market.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Money spent on machinery and buildings is ________ capital. (b) Money spent on raw materials, wages and rent is ________ capital.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain briefly feasibility study and identifying entrepreneurial opportunities as functions of an entrepreneur.
questions.answer:
Identifying opportunities: sensing changing human needs (food, fashion, education) faster than others and finding a business in them — the first function.
Feasibility study: studying whether the proposed product will succeed — market demand, inputs, costs, sources and problems — and preparing a business plan or project report.

questions.q: Write a short note on entrepreneurship.
questions.answer: Entrepreneurship is the process of identifying an opportunity, turning the idea into an enterprise, arranging resources, managing it and bearing its risk. It creates employment and wealth, encourages innovation and helps the development of the nation.

questions.q: State two points of importance of entrepreneurship.
questions.answer:
(1) It provides employment to the entrepreneur and others and reduces unemployment.
(2) It creates wealth and new products, contributing to research and national development.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: How would motivation help an entrepreneur in running a small business?
questions.answer:
(1) It gives him the drive to keep working until the goal is reached, even in difficulties.
(2) It keeps him enthusiastic about improving products and service.
(3) A motivated owner inspires his employees, which raises their output and loyalty.

questions.q: How can small enterprises contribute to national development?
questions.answer:
(1) They provide employment to a large number of people with little capital.
(2) They use local resources and skills and promote balanced regional development.
(3) They add to production and exports and lead to a fairer distribution of income.

or.q: Why is decision-making ability important for an entrepreneur?
or.answer: An entrepreneur must take many decisions — what to produce, where, how much, at what price. Right and timely decisions help him seize opportunities before others, avoid losses and keep the business growing; delay can mean a missed opportunity and loss.

questions.q: What are the sources of finance for setting up a small business?
questions.answer:
(1) Own savings (self-contribution).
(2) Loans from friends and relatives.
(3) Loans from banks and financial institutions, and government schemes such as MUDRA and SIDBI.

questions.q: State any three qualities of a successful entrepreneur.
questions.answer:
(1) Initiative — taking prompt action on opportunities.
(2) Willingness to take risk.
(3) Self-confidence and decision-making ability.

or.q: What factors would you consider if you start a small enterprise to produce paper cups?
or.answer:
(1) Finance — fixed capital for machines and working capital for paper and wages.
(2) Location — near suppliers of paper and near the market (hotels, tea stalls), with power and transport.
(3) Availability of labour, technology and machinery; demand in the market; legal formalities.

questions.q: Describe any four qualities of a successful entrepreneur.
questions.answer: (1) Initiative. (2) Willingness to assume risk. (3) Ability to learn from experience. (4) Motivation. (Also self-confidence and decision-making ability.)

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is entrepreneurship? Explain any four functions of an entrepreneur.
questions.answer:
Entrepreneurship is the process of identifying a business opportunity and creating and managing an enterprise to exploit it, bearing the risk involved.
(1) Identifying opportunities — spotting unmet needs in the market.
(2) Feasibility study — studying demand, costs and inputs and preparing a business plan.
(3) Resourcing — arranging finance, machines, materials and people.
(4) Setting up and managing the enterprise — legal formalities, location, production, finance and marketing.
(5) Growth and development — setting higher goals and striving for excellence.

or.q: What factors would you consider if you start a small enterprise to produce bathing soap?
or.answer:
(1) Finance — fixed capital (machines, premises) and working capital (oils, chemicals, wages).
(2) Line of business — demand for soap, competition, profitability.
(3) Form of organisation — sole proprietorship or partnership.
(4) Location — near raw-material suppliers and the market, with transport, water and power.
(5) Labour, technology, legal formalities (licences, quality marks) and marketing.

questions.q: Explain any five factors you would consider while setting up a small business.
questions.answer:
(1) Arrangement of finance — fixed and working capital from savings, relatives and banks.
(2) Selection of the line of business — demand, profitability and risk.
(3) Choice of form of organisation — sole proprietorship or partnership.
(4) Location — raw material, market, labour, transport and banking.
(5) Availability of labour and technology; legal formalities and marketing.

or.q: Who is an entrepreneur? Explain any four functions of an entrepreneur.
or.answer:
An entrepreneur is a person who identifies a business opportunity, sets up and manages an enterprise and bears its risk.
Functions: identifying opportunities; turning ideas into action and feasibility study; resourcing; setting up and managing the enterprise; growth and development.

questions.q: Vivek, a finance manager, decides to start his own business. Explain five qualities he should have to be a successful entrepreneur.
questions.answer:
(1) Initiative — act quickly on opportunities.
(2) Willingness to take calculated risk.
(3) Ability to learn from experience.
(4) Motivation and hard work.
(5) Self-confidence and decision-making ability.

questions.q: State any six functions of an entrepreneur.
questions.answer:
(1) Identifying entrepreneurial opportunities.
(2) Turning ideas into action.
(3) Feasibility study and business plan.
(4) Resourcing — money, machines, materials, men.
(5) Setting up the enterprise.
(6) Managing the enterprise.
(7) Growth and development (with innovation and risk bearing).

questions.q: What factors would you consider if you start a small enterprise to produce wrist watches? Explain four.
questions.answer:
(1) Finance — sizeable fixed capital for precision machinery and working capital for parts and wages.
(2) Location — near suppliers of components and the market, with skilled labour and good transport.
(3) Skilled labour and technology for precision assembly.
(4) Demand and competition, form of organisation, legal formalities and marketing.
